Chart   Why it works   What to plot   Best manager use

Stacked column chart by month   Shows total monthly revenue and mix shift at the same time   X-axis: month; Y-axis: revenue; stacks: North Standard, South Standard, North Premium, South Premium   Spot whether growth came from one segment or was broad-based

Dual-line chart for units and revenue by month   Reveals whether revenue is growing with volume or through mix/price changes   X-axis: month; Lines: total revenue and total units   Check if revenue growth is volume-led, premium-mix-led, or both
- For the stacked column chart, use   revenue  , not units, because monthly review discussions usually start with topline contribution.
- For the dual-line chart, put   revenue on the left axis   and   units on the right axis   so both trends remain readable.
Manager Checks: 5 Specific Insights to Look For
1.   March is the clear acceleration month
- Revenue rose from   119,500 to 130,000   from February to March.
- This suggests a real business lift, not just pricing noise.
2.   North Standard is the main growth engine
- This segment is both largest and steadily expanding, so it deserves close attention for capacity, retention, and margin protection.
3.   South Standard dipped in February, then rebounded strongly in March
- The manager should check whether February had a temporary issue such as inventory, sales coverage, or seasonality.
4.   North Premium softened in February and only partially recovered
- This may indicate weaker premium demand in the North versus stronger execution elsewhere.
5.   South Premium is the strongest improving premium segment
- The manager should investigate what is working here—sales motion, pricing, promotions, or customer mix—and consider replicating it.

-   Early signals of mix change across Standard vs Premium
